driver_note:
Playwright still cannot launch on this host (chromium.launch() times out at 180s at 0% CPU; the macOS XPC services it and the Metal shader compiler share are wedged). Every check was executed as the equivalent DOM query through an already-open Chrome against the running app, in tabs created for this run. Four-width sweep run in a same-origin iframe sized to 1440/1100/860/700 CSS px so window.innerWidth really was the target and the 820px media query on .dis-sides evaluated against it.

BUNDLE — AND THE STALE-BUNDLE TRAP FIRED AGAIN, MID-RUN. Pinned before the first assertion: assets/index-S8nzILcC.js, sha256 82f9a3635551bb57 over 454574 bytes, matching frontend/dist. The whole suite was run and passed against it. On the closing re-pin the in-page no-store fetch of that same URL returned 22 bytes — the API's {"detail":"Not Found"} body — while the CSS still served 200. Cause: a concurrent agent rebuilt the frontend at 14:41, replacing index-S8nzILcC.js with index-DC5ijKw3.js; the CSS filename is content-identical across builds (index-CjtTw7_q.css throughout) so it kept serving, which is what made the failure look selective rather than like a rebuild. Rather than mix observations, EVERY check was re-executed end to end against the new bundle — index-DC5ijKw3.js, sha256 e16540f3029c5378 over 459136 bytes, verified against disk before and after, and stable across the re-run. Both bundles produced identical results on every check. frontend/src/pipeline/DisagreementsView.tsx is unchanged from HEAD (mtime 14:15, predating both rebuilds), so the rebuilds came from the concurrent scoreboard work. A transient note worth recording for operators: between the rebuild and a server restart, http://127.0.0.1:8021/ served an index.html naming an asset the running process could no longer produce, so a reader loading the app in that window got a blank page. That is an artifact of rebuilding under a long-running server, not a defect in this layer.

The real .yt-agent/conflicts.json was read but never modified. No second instance was needed this run; 8021 was never restarted.
notes: BOTH FAILURES ARE NOW CLOSED AND V7 PASSES. The gate: 7 cross-channel conflicts against >=3. The error bar: the artifact carries count_sd_estimate 1.37 and the headline renders '7 disagreements ± 1.4' with '6 firm · 9 pairs undecided' and the observed sub-run line 'the same data yields 7, 6, 10 disagreements'. Not re-adjudicated by me — the provider is still 402 and this evaluation needed zero model calls.

THE RETIRE CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP. I wrote it against a synthetic artifact because no real one carried the stability fields; this is the first real build to have them, and .dis-caveat is absent at all four widths while the measured ± renders. The fallback did not outlive the gap it covered. Every one of the three renderings the spread check accepts has now been exercised: stated-caveat on the 3-look artifact, measured ± on this one, observed sub-runs on both this one and the synthetic.

undecided_pairs RENDERS 9, so the float fix is visible where it matters. The chip reads '6 firm · 9 pairs undecided' in warn styling (warn because firm 6 != count 7). I did not re-derive the fix, but the rendered 9 is consistent with 27 minority verdicts and with 6 of 7 cards sitting below unanimity, and a rendered '0 pairs undecided' beside 27 minority verdicts would have been the visible symptom of the bug.

THE REGIME IS UNMISTAKABLE, AND THE 3-LOOK SPECIAL-CASING CORRECTLY DOES NOT FIRE. The statline prints '× 9 looks each = 6390 calls'; card chips read 'agreed 9/9 looks' (green) for the unanimous card and 'split — only N of 9 looks' (warn) for the other six. No .dis-taglist chip contains the string 'the most' — checked per-element, not by scanning body text, because card 6's axis legitimately contains 'the most annoying/repetitive part of their work' and a naive body-text scan reports that as the special-case firing.

NEAR-MISSES STILL UNREACHABLE, and the surface got larger in two ways this build: 25 near-misses (up from 11) and a NEW 710-entry vote_ledger carrying chunk ids and vote counts for every candidate pair. Neither is forwarded: list_conflicts returns a nine-key dict (the eight from before plus corpus), and the payload the page itself received confirms it — no near_misses, no vote_ledger. The served bundle contains zero occurrences of near_miss/nearMiss/vote_ledger/voteLedger, as does frontend/src. A DOM sweep with the calibration strip expanded found none of the 47 distinct near-miss chunk ids and none of the near-miss axes as exact strings.

ONE APPARENT LEAK, RUN DOWN AND DISMISSED — recorded because it is exactly the finding that would be misreported. My first sweep used 38-character axis prefixes and returned two hits. Both landed in .dis-axis of SHIPPED cards, and both are prefix collisions: the near-miss axis "Should the term 'non-functional requirements' be used?" is a proper prefix of shipped card 1's "...be used as a category in requirements discussions?", and similarly for the job-seekers axis. No near-miss axis is exactly equal to any shipped axis, the pairs are different (near-miss chunk:4qfsmE11Ejo:47+iJLL-KPqBpM:2 at 3/9 versus the shipped chunk:4qfsmE11Ejo:47+iJLL-KPqBpM:1), and the text on screen belongs entirely to the pair that won. Three chunk ids appear in both a near-miss pair and a shipped card, which is expected since a chunk can be in several candidate pairs — and irrelevant to the UI, because chunk ids render nowhere at all.

THE NEW corpus FIELD RENDERS HONESTLY, and closes a gap I flagged in both previous verdicts. Chip: 'over 71 videos / 1792 chunks · 00813df8', tooltip 'The corpus this count was taken over, digested over chunk id and text. Two runs are only comparable if this matches.' It states the population, shows the digest a reader would need to compare two runs, truncates it visibly rather than implying the full value, and does not overclaim — it says what the count was measured over, not that the corpus is complete. The artifact also carries chunks_with_claims 1749 / videos_with_claims 71, which are not rendered; that is a defensible omission rather than a misleading one.

OBSERVATION, NOT A FAILURE — a vocabulary mismatch between the header and the cards. The header says '6 firm' using FIRM_VOTE_SHARE (>=2/3 of looks), while a card chip goes green only at full unanimity, so six of seven cards wear an amber 'split — only N of 9 looks' including the 8/9 and 6/9 cards that the header counts as firm. A reader is told six are firm and cannot tell from the cards which six. This errs toward under-confidence, which is the safe direction and the opposite of the defect I originally raised, so I am not counting it against the slice — but the two vocabularies are measuring different things under labels that read as if they measure the same thing.

Probe repeats are now 3 while corpus pairs get 9, inverting the asymmetry the first v7 verdict recorded. That earlier version was serious because the strip certified a stability the cards had not been given; this inversion is the benign direction — the calibration strip is now the weaker measurement, so it understates rather than overstates what the cards are worth. Recorded, not counted.

Carried forward unchanged: the 'no winner language' scan still deliberately excludes .dis-factual, because extending it there fires on 'settle' and would report an explicit refusal to pick a winner as winner language. Re-read by hand on this build across all 7 cards; no card names a side.
